clue.text: Police discover one in lake after danger is dispersed

indicators.note: letters dispersed are scattered about and so land in a new order
one sits in the lake, so its letter goes inside the word for it

parts.note: a mere is a small lake
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Police find a body in a lake once a dangerous situation has calmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the lake-and-one piece behind GENDAR, the anagram of DANGER. 'in' puts I inside MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gendarmerie is the French armed police force.

clue.text: Set up Crete when it is in turmoil

indicators.note: a word in turmoil is thrown into confusion, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something was founded on the island of Crete during a period of unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turmoil' rearranges CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect is to build or raise a structure upright.

clue.text: Finishing level although getting victory in the fancy dress?

indicators.note: the victory sits in the fancy dress, so its letters go inside

parts.note: drag is flamboyant costume, especially women's clothes worn by a man as a performance
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: A contest ends all square even though someone in costume seemed to triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts WIN inside DRAG; the question mark flags the loose sense of drag as fancy dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn game is one where the sides finish with equal scores.

clue.text: Where we hear one who moves quickly

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a rusher is someone who dashes about

explanation.surface: A question about the place where a speedy person is to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' sounds out RUSHER, which in a non-rhotic British accent is said like the country. The bare 'Where' is a deliberately vague definition: a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is a country, so it answers the question of location.

clue.text: Providing a job for the attractive

definitions.meaning: to engage someone is to hire them

explanation.surface: Employing somebody because they are good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking on a worker is employing them, and a winning, charming manner is called this too.

clue.text: The whole is turning it green

indicators.note: something turning changes its form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Everything is changing colour to green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is turning' rearranges IT GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, with no fractional part.

clue.text: One who draws out capital for a tourist attraction

definitions.text: One who draws out capital for a tourist attraction

parts.words: One who draws out capital for a tourist attraction
parts.note: read 'draws' as hauls: a hauler who drags the British capital along, which names a famous fortress on the Thames

explanation.surface: A bank customer withdraws money to fund a visitor attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws out capital' looks like taking money from a bank; instead a tower is a vehicle that tows, and the capital is London.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous fortress by the Thames is one of Britain's most visited sights.

clue.text: Peasants went on parade without exclamation

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the parade phrase goes around the exclamation

parts.note: soldiers fell in when they lined up on parade
ah is a cry of surprise

explanation.surface: Farm workers marched in a parade without saying a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, putting FELL IN around AH.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellahin are peasant farmers of Egypt and the Arab world.

clue.text: Media activity undertaken to urge river god to hold a soldier up

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: one piece holds another, so it wraps around it

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Newspapers urge a river god to hoist a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GI into IG, and 'to hold' puts it inside PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A press campaign is a sustained push by newspapers for a cause.

clue.text: The final one among home games

indicators.note: among says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The last match of the season is played at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' points into HOME GAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence a byword for the end.

clue.text: As a tourist she gets involved with tigers

indicators.note: the two words get mixed up together, their letters jumbled into one

explanation.surface: A woman on holiday has an encounter with tigers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved with' mixes SHE and TIGERS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer visits places of interest, as any holidaymaker does.

clue.text: Necessitating being ill after being given some medicine

indicators.note: after places the being-ill piece behind the medicine piece

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a branch of medicine
ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone sick is prescribed some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts AILING behind ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to involve it as a necessary consequence.

clue.text: Makes a fool of birds

definitions.meaning: to gull someone is to dupe them

explanation.surface: Seabirds playing tricks on people.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to trick them; the same word names common seabirds.

clue.text: Something to eat produced by an appeal to the cooker

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
a range is a large kitchen stove

explanation.surface: A meal comes from a plea to the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as 'O, Range!', a cry addressed to the cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: This citrus fruit is eaten fresh or juiced.

clue.text: Creature makes one grow excessively fond as a cure

parts.note: an ant is a small creature
the Roman numeral for one is I
to dote is to be foolishly fond

explanation.surface: A creature's devotion acts as a healing remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that counteracts a poison is called this.

clue.text: A broken chair can become chaotic

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A smashed piece of furniture can make a room disorderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges CHAIR CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means lawless and disorderly.

clue.text: A girl whon the horse went round held firm

indicators.note: the horse goes round the other pieces, so it encloses them

parts.note: a steed is a horse
Di is short for Diana, a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl rode round on a horse and kept her balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went round' puts STEED around A and DI. 'whon' is a misprint for 'whom' in the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadied means kept stable, made steady.

clue.text: Left it with a single means of entry to contest at law

parts.note: one, the Roman numeral I
a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: Someone departed by a lone gate to go to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to take a dispute to a court.

clue.text: The police leave carrying spoilt tapes

indicators.note: one word carries the other, so it holds it within

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: spoilt tapes are damaged, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Officers go off with damaged recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' rearranges TAPES as ESTAP; 'carrying' puts that inside GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the Nazi secret state police.

clue.text: A hero perhaps, he takes me back without a mount

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the reversed piece goes around the mount
back means the word me is read in reverse

parts.note: a pony is a horse to ride

explanation.surface: A hero goes home with nothing to ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME into EM; 'without' (outside) puts EM around PONY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero who gives his name to a work or place, like Hamlet, is this.

clue.text: Knock up those who have the talent for a story

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to rap is to knock
the able are those with ability

explanation.surface: Gifted people wake someone up to tell them a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAP into PAR. 'Knock up' is British for waking someone by knocking on their door.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral tale.

clue.text: Universal wit embraces skinhead

indicators.note: one word embraces another, so it hugs it inside

parts.note: a comic is a funny person, a wit
the head of skin, its first letter

explanation.surface: A joker hugs a shaven-headed youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' is split as head of 'skin', giving S; 'embraces' puts it inside COMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic means relating to the whole universe.

clue.text: Knotty points found in a: number of poems

parts.note: odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: Difficult questions crop up in a collection of poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodes are knots or joints, points where things are tied or meet.

clue.text: Secrets which may make the artillery company happy

indicators.note: the pieces may make a new word when their letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Hidden things that could cheer up a gunnery unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which may make' rearranges RA, CO and HAPPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Apocrypha are writings of doubtful authority, once held to be hidden or secret.

clue.text: Former church leader

definitions.meaning: the head of a priory, below an abbot

explanation.surface: An ex-head of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier in time is one sense; a monk in charge of a religious house is the other.

clue.text: Potty banishment?

parts.note: in ancient Athens citizens voted to exile someone by scratching names on broken pottery shards, so the exile was literally pot-made

explanation.surface: A crazy expulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like crazy, but means to do with pots: the Greek votes were cast on potsherds.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusion from a group, named after the Athenian vote of exile.

clue.text: Fetch an extra symbol of union

parts.note: in cricket a bye, written B, is an extra run
a wedding ring symbolises marriage

explanation.surface: Bring along an extra wedding band.
explanation.walkthrough: B stands for bye, a cricket extra: a run scored without the batter hitting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something is to carry it here, to fetch it.

clue.text: I weep about a girl beside the water in india

indicators.note: beside places the water next to the other pieces

parts.note: a pond is a body of water

indicators.note: the weeping goes about the girl, enclosing her

parts.note: to cry is to weep
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: Someone weeps over a girl by the water in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HER inside CRY, giving CHERRY; the pond goes in front of I and that.
explanation.definitionFit: Pondicherry, now Puducherry, is a former French territory and city in India.
